title: Site morphisms, associated-representable comparisons and the orientation
statement: With the large triple-site data of [def-trf-large-oriented-site-data], a continuous finite-limit-preserving functor H:C→T induces the geometric morphism from Sh(T) to Sh(C), and its inverse image takes U^a naturally to H(U)^a, in independent universes. Suppose geometric projections p1,p2 with their displayed associated-representable comparisons pi1,pi2 are given. If the associated middle-to-first arrows are invertible, there exists an orientation tau:(gp2)_*→(fp1)_* satisfying LargeOrientationFormula. No universality or existence of lifts is asserted.

proof.text: Representable flatness follows from finite-limit preservation. The continuous sheaf pullback and pushforward have their canonical adjunction; flatness and exact filtered colimits of sets make the inverse image left exact. This constructs largeSiteMorphism with real data.

Compose the site adjunction with the sheafification adjunction. Its right adjoint is precomposition followed by the sheaf inclusion, equally the right adjoint to left Kan extension followed by sheafification. Uniqueness of left adjoints, and the Kan-extension formula on lifted Yoneda representables, give largeAssociatedComparison. The two possible ULift universe parameters are identified by the explicit up/down isomorphism.

Apply [lem-trf-large-oriented-representable-comparison] to the transformation on associated representables constructed in the next step. It gives a unique direct-image transformation, and its mate is the specified transformation on each associated representable.

The middle triples and structural arrows are functorial. After association invert the middle-to-first natural transformation and compose with the middle-to-second one. Transport along etaF, etaG, pi1 and pi2. Apply the preceding direct-image construction and its mate calculation. Its component is exactly LargeOrientationFormula.
